analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | A&D | chemicals | housing 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: S&P futures up 15bps toward all-time highs with deep dispersion under the surface. Bank earnings start Q3'26 this week, with CPI on Wednesday as the main data event.

Reaction was calm to weekend attacks on the Saudi capital's main airports, despite concern about a wider conflict. Brent is $105, WTI $92, European natural gas $83 (+2%), corn $4.82 spot, Bitcoin $86.5k.
Consumer sentiment data from Friday shows current conditions at all-time lows.

Prime brokerage: after five straight weeks of selling US Industrials (6 of the last 7), hedge funds net bought the sector at the fastest pace since early January (+1.8 SDs over 1 year), almost entirely through long buys. Aerospace & Defense, Construction & Engineering, Airlines and Industrial Conglomerates were the most net bought. The long/short ratio is 1.73, the 15th percentile vs the past year and the 22nd vs the past five years.

FAST reports 10/14 pre-market with a 6% implied move. The stock has fallen on earnings four quarters in a row. Consensus revenue growth looks a tough high for Q3 but reasonable for Q4. Gross margin looks in line for Q3 and perhaps a touch high for Q4. EBIT looks too high in both quarters. Short interest is 36mm shares (24mm a year ago, 6 days to cover). The desk rates positioning 3/10 (1 = most crowded short, 10 = most crowded long).

FAST has outperformed since mid July as inflation expectations rose (de-escalating Middle East tensions, higher rates, a Fed rate hike). Distributors can capture gross margin benefits before inflation reaches their costs.

JBHT reports 10/15 post-market with a 6% implied move. The stock fell from $270-280 to $230 after the company flagged Q3 EPS that could be down sequentially. Sell-side Q3 EPS estimates are about $1.83 (down 4% sequentially). Consensus calls for 35% EPS growth next year after 20% this year. Valuation is 24x PE and 11x EV/EBITDA on a blended NTM basis. Short interest has halved to 2mm shares. The desk rates positioning 4/10.

A&D Q3'26 preview: the desk likes aerospace aftermarket (concerns priced in, expects strong 3Q and positive 2027 commentary). It sees continued risk of slower pace in aero OE, solid but slower business jet growth, and a debate over medium-term growth and margins in defense. Government IT demand is expected to stay slow.

Boeing 737 MAX deliveries averaged about 41 a month this summer (41 Aug, 39 Jul, 42 Jun). The plan to stabilize at 47/month is taking longer than expected. 787 output is stable at 8/month, but the engine deliveries needed to reach 10/month have not been achieved.

Aerospace aftermarket: airlines are not changing fleets despite fuel prices because they can pass costs on and are short of new aircraft. Pent-up maintenance demand is substantial, and pricing is above its historical average.

Defense large caps are de-rating while revenue grows. They may be near peak DoD budget authorization on tough baseline comparisons, and the Pentagon is pushing more risk sharing into contract terms. The desk still sees growth and margin pockets, such as Navy.

Chemicals: 3Q26 is shaping up below consensus, with more risk of misses than beats. The Middle East conflict was less bullish for basic chemicals than expected because of alternate supply (e.g., China) and demand destruction.

Polyethylene: July settled down 10 c/lb after a 15 c/lb cut in June. August settled flat, but CMA applied a net market adjustment of down 5 c/lb. September has not settled as of 10/9, with participants hoping for +3-5 c/lb.
PVC prices rose 18% sequentially in 2Q and fell about 2% in 3Q. The desk expects a 2-4% decline in 4Q and a 3-5% rebound in 2027.
Methanol contract prices fell in September on flat seasonal demand and ample supply. US Gulf Coast MTBE supply tightened on a major plant outage.

Housing: the desk expects moderation in 3Q results. The 30-year mortgage rate is up 74bps since August, in the low-to-mid 7% range, and consumer confidence is weak. Inflation is adding price/cost pressure. 52% of coverage trades within 5% of its 52-week lows, and seasonality suggests upside into year-end.

The desk cut its 2026 single-family starts forecast to 900k (-4.6% YoY) from 920k, and multi-family to 420k from 432k. Total starts are 1.319mn (-2.9%). It raised its R&R forecast to +6.7% for 2026 and +2.0% for 2027, from +3.1% and +0.9%, with price up 5.9% and volume up 0.8% in 2026.

earnings_insights: FAST: reports Wednesday 10/14 pre-market (7am, call at 10am), implied move 6%. Down on earnings four quarters in a row. Consensus revenue growth looks a tough high for Q3, EBIT too high in Q3 and Q4. These are consensus estimates, not reported figures.

JBHT: reports Thursday 10/15 post-market at 4:05pm (call at 5pm), implied move 6%. Sell-side Q3 EPS estimate is about $1.83 (consensus estimate, not reported), down 4% sequentially. The stock rose 8% in Q2'26 and 6% in Q1'26 on earnings.
Chemicals: 3Q26 is tracking below consensus with more risk of misses than beats. The desk updated its estimates for mark-to-market commodity pricing.

Housing: Q3 results are expected to be more muted than the better-than-expected 2Q (share gains, product innovation, cost actions, tariff refunds). 4Q/2026 guides are likely to be modestly narrowed at or slightly below the lower end of prior ranges.
Bogeys (investor questions) being gathered: FAST ADS/gross margins, PCAR TP&O gross margins, NVT orders, MMM organic growth.
